main_body: Multi-storey school building drawn as a flat front facade: rows of windows and a glass entrance door on a cream wall, topped by a green rooftop garden panel with rooftop units, bordered by a pale parapet.
top_band: Rows 7-37 are a green roof surface (L about 115) inside a pale parapet (rows 1-5, L 158-226). The roof is drawn as a flat rectangular plane facing the viewer, with no foreshortening or depth, so it reads like a vertical panel. It is not a separate top band over a front face.
evidence: The facade is a pure front elevation. The windows, door, floor bands and brick base are all painted on a vertical plane. The green roof is about 38 rows tall, nearly as tall as one or two storeys, so it is a flat garden panel drawn face-on and not a foreshortened top. The parapet is a 1-5 row rim with a thin lip, which is too thin to read as a top surface. There is no short top band sitting above a separate front face, and no eave shadow or inset door. The windows have only slight frames and the door has a dark frame, but the building as a whole is not a 3/4 piece. Fails as front elevation.

style.evidence: The measured facts put the candidate at 10 colours per tile, close to the stone reference at 11 and below the timber house at 18. Its 43 distinct colours are well under the references' 66 and 185. Flat-fill coverage is 12% against 0% for both references, which shows in the plain cream wall areas and the large window glass. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines are tinted and read as material tones. The green roof has clumps in several greens, and the wall has speckle. Even so, the cream wall bands and the window panes are repetitive and flatter than the references, which shade each stone and tile individually. It would look thinner next to them, so it fails.
